title: Grammatical Gender & Hard/Soft Noun Patterns
subtitle: Determine Czech noun genders and base endings at a glance
keyPoint: Czech nouns fall into masculine, feminine, or neuter genders, largely identifiable by their basic nominative singular endings.

examples.en: Ta nová kniha je velmi zajímavá.

mistakes.note: Nouns ending in -a are almost always feminine and require feminine demonstratives.
Nouns ending in -o are neuter and take the pronoun 'to'.
Nouns ending in consonants are masculine, taking 'ten'.

quiz.question: Identify the feminine noun: 'Here is a ___.'
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -a like 'káva' (coffee) are feminine.

quiz.question: Which word is neuter (taking 'to')?
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -o such as 'město' are grammatically neuter.

quiz.question: Choose the masculine inanimate noun:
quiz.explanation: 'Dům' (house) ends in a consonant and is masculine inanimate.

quiz.question: Which ending is typical for neuter nouns?
quiz.explanation: The vowel ending -o is the classic standard marker for neuter nouns.

tip: Look at the last letter: -a is feminine, -o/-e/-í is neuter, and a consonant is masculine.

title: Present Tense Verb Conjugation Classes
subtitle: Conjugate Czech verbs across the main vowel-stem groups
keyPoint: Czech verbs conjugate by removing the infinitive suffix -t and adding personal endings based on their stem vowel class.

examples.en: Každé ráno snídám chléb a sýr.

mistakes.note: Verbs must drop the infinitive -t and take personal endings like -m for 'já'.
Verbs ending in -ovat change to -uj- plus person endings like -eme for 'my'.
The suffix -te belongs to 'vy' (you plural/formal), whereas 'oni' takes -í for this class.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form of 'dělat' for 'my' (we): 'My ___ oběd.'
quiz.explanation: The first-person plural ending for the -á class is -áme ('děláme').

quiz.question: Choose the correct form of 'studovat' for 'on' (he): 'On ___ medicínu.'
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular for -ovat verbs takes -uje ('studuje').

quiz.question: Complete for 'já' (I) with 'rozumět': 'Já dobře ___.'
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular suffix for this class is -ím ('rozumím').

quiz.question: Complete for 'vy' (formal you) with 'mluvit': 'Odkud ___?'
quiz.explanation: The second-person plural/polite ending is -íte ('mluvíte').

tip: Verbs ending in -ovat almost universally conjugate as -uju, -uješ, -uje, -ujeme, -ujete, -ujou/-ují.

title: Accusative Singular & Masculine Animacy
subtitle: Master direct objects and the animate vs. inanimate split
keyPoint: In the accusative singular, feminine -a changes to -u, neuters stay unchanged, and masculine animates gain -a while inanimates do not change.

examples.en: Mám rád černou kávu bez cukru.

mistakes.note: Direct objects of feminine nouns in -a change to -u in the accusative case.
Masculine animate nouns must take the accusative ending -a.
Masculine inanimate nouns remain identical to their nominative forms.

quiz.question: Complete the direct object: 'Mám rád ___ (pizza).'
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -a shift to -u in the accusative singular.

quiz.question: Complete with masculine animate: 'Hledám ___ (kolega).'
quiz.explanation: Masculine animate nouns ending in -a inflect like feminine nouns in the accusative, taking -u.

quiz.question: Complete with masculine inanimate: 'Mám nový ___ (telefon).'
quiz.explanation: Masculine inanimate nouns keep the nominative form in accusative singular.

quiz.question: Complete with masculine animate: 'Čekám na ___ (bratr).'
quiz.explanation: Hard masculine animate nouns add -a in the accusative singular.

tip: Only feminine -a and masculine animates shift visibly in the accusative singular; neuters and inanimate masculines look identical to nominative.

title: Past Tense and the Auxiliary Verb 'být'
subtitle: Form compound past actions with l-participles and clitics
keyPoint: The past tense pairs an l-participle agreeing in gender and number with the present auxiliary of 'být' (omitted entirely in the 3rd person).

useCases.label: Group Activity
useCases.example: Minulý týden jsme byli v kině.

examples.en: Minulý rok jsme cestovali do Itálie.

mistakes.note: Never use 'je' as a past auxiliary in the 3rd person; the participle stands alone.
In the 1st person, the auxiliary 'jsem' is required to mark past tense.
The l-participle must match feminine gender by appending -a ('byla').

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 'ty' (to a female): 'Kde ___ včera?'
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person feminine uses the auxiliary 'jsi' and feminine ending -a ('jsi byla').

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 3rd person masculine: 'Petr včera ___ fotbal.'
quiz.explanation: Third person past tense does not use any form of the auxiliary 'být'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 'já' (male speaker): 'Včera ___ dlouho.'
quiz.explanation: A male speaker says '(já) jsem spal' using the auxiliary 'jsem' and masculine ending -l.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for 'my' (we): 'V sobotu ___ na výlet.'
quiz.explanation: 'My' requires the auxiliary 'jsme' together with the plural participle 'jeli'.

tip: The auxiliary forms 'jsem, jsi, jsme, jste' are clitics and typically occupy the second grammatical slot in the clause.

title: Locative Singular with Static Prepositions
subtitle: Indicate static locations and topics using 'v', 'na', and 'o'
keyPoint: The locative is the only Czech case that strictly requires a preposition (such as 'v', 'na', or 'o') to express location or topic.

mistakes.note: Preposition 'v' demands the locative; -h/-ch/-k mutate before -e (h->z: Praha -> Praze).
Static location after 'na' triggers locative ending -e, not nominative/accusative.
Masculine animate nouns take the locative singular ending -ovi when talking 'about' them.

quiz.question: Complete the static location: 'Petr bydlí v ___ (Brno).'
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns ending in -o mutate to -ě/-e in the locative singular ('v Brně').

quiz.question: Complete with consonant mutation: 'Jsme v ___ (Praha).'
quiz.explanation: Stem-final 'h' mutates to 'z' before the locative ending -e ('v Praze').

quiz.question: Complete the topic: 'Mluvíme o ___ (škola).'
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in hard consonants + -a take -e/-ě in the locative ('o škole').

quiz.question: Complete the location: 'Čaj je na ___ (stůl).'
quiz.explanation: 'Stůl' takes the soft locative ending -e, accompanied by vowel shortening ('na stole').

tip: Remember: The locative NEVER stands alone in Czech without a preposition like 'v', 'na', 'o', or 'po'.

title: Modal Verbs and Negation
subtitle: Express ability, obligation, and permission with conjugated modals followed by an infinitive
keyPoint: Conjugate the modal verb to match the subject and attach 'ne-' directly to negate it, followed by the main verb in the infinitive.

examples.en: Dnes večer nemůžu přijít na večeři.

mistakes.note: The secondary verb following a modal must always be in the infinitive (-t ending), not conjugated.
In Czech, verbal negation prefix 'ne-' is written joined directly to the verb without spaces.
'Nesmět' expresses strict prohibition (you must not), whereas lack of necessity (you don't have to) requires 'nemuset'.

quiz.question: I cannot understand you.
quiz.explanation: Physical or cognitive inability is expressed by the negated form of 'moci/moct' ('nemůžu').

quiz.question: You do not have to pay here.
quiz.explanation: 'You do not have to' expresses absence of obligation, which requires 'nemusíš'.

quiz.question: We want to learn Czech.
quiz.explanation: 'We want' corresponds to 1st person plural of chtít ('chceme') followed by the infinitive 'učit se'.

quiz.question: Children may not drink beer.
quiz.explanation: 'May not' (prohibition by rule) requires 'nesmějí' from the verb 'smět'.

tip: Remember the distinction between 'nemusíš' (you don't have to / optional) and 'nesmíš' (you must not / forbidden) — mixing them up changes permission into a command!

title: Verbal Aspect: Imperfective vs. Perfective
subtitle: Distinguish continuous/repeated actions from one-off, completed results
keyPoint: Imperfective verbs focus on ongoing duration or repetition, while perfective verbs view an action as a completed whole with an outcome.

useCases.label: Ongoing Process
useCases.example: Včera jsem celý večer psal dopis.

examples.en: Dlouho vařila polévku pro celou rodinu.
Dočetl tu knihu až do konce.

mistakes.wrong: Už jsem psal ten úkol a je hotový.
mistakes.right: Už jsem napsal ten úkol a je hotový.
mistakes.note: If the action reached completion and resulted in a finished product, use the perfective 'napsat'.

mistakes.wrong: Včera jsem dvě hodiny přečetl knihu.
mistakes.right: Včera jsem dvě hodiny četl knihu.
mistakes.note: Durational expressions with 'how long' (dvě hodiny) require the imperfective aspect ('četl').

mistakes.wrong: Každý den udělám snídani pro děti.
mistakes.right: Každý den dělám snídani pro děti.
mistakes.note: Habitual repeated everyday actions ('každý den') require the imperfective present ('dělám').

quiz.question: Yesterday I was reading a book the whole evening. (Process)
options: Včera jsem celý večer přečetl knihu.
Včera jsem celý večer četl knihu.
Včera jsem celý večer dočetl knihu.
quiz.explanation: 'Celý večer' indicates duration and ongoing process, which requires the imperfective past tense 'četl'.

quiz.question: Have you already finished doing your homework?
quiz.explanation: The question targets the completed result of the action, demanding the perfective past form 'udělal'.

quiz.question: We regularly buy bread here. (Habit)
quiz.explanation: Repeated regular actions ('pravidelně') require the imperfective verb 'kupovat' in the present tense ('kupujeme').

quiz.question: Martin finally solved the problem.
quiz.explanation: 'Konečně' (finally) combined with the attainment of a result calls for the perfective verb 'vyřešit'.

tip: Time markers provide the best clue: 'celý den', 'dlouho', and 'často' trigger imperfective, while 'najednou', 'hned', and 'už' usually pair with perfective.

title: Future Tense Formation by Aspect
subtitle: Use compound future for imperfective verbs and present forms for perfective verbs
keyPoint: Imperfective future uses forms of 'být' plus the infinitive (budu dělat), whereas perfective verbs express the future automatically using their present conjugation (udělám).

examples.en: Až přijdu domů, hned ti zavolám.
Co budeš dělat v sobotu dopoledne?
V létě se budu učit německy.

mistakes.right: Zítra napíšu dopis. / Zítra budu psát dopis.
mistakes.note: Never combine 'budu' with a perfective infinitive; either use 'budu psát' or simply 'napíšu'.

mistakes.wrong: Teď udělám úkol. (meaning 'I am doing it right now')
mistakes.note: Present forms of perfective verbs always indicate future time in Czech, never the immediate present.
Verbs of motion like 'jít' and 'jet' have unique prefix-based futures ('půjdu', 'pojedeš') rather than taking 'budu'.

quiz.question: Tomorrow I will be watching TV all evening.
options: Zítra se podívám na televizi celý večer.
Zítra se budu dívat na televizi celý večer.
Zítra se dívám na televizi celý večer.
Zítra budu se podívat na televizi celý večer.
quiz.explanation: Continuous future action over a long duration ('celý večer') demands compound future 'budu se dívat'.

quiz.question: I will buy milk on the way home. (One completed event)
quiz.explanation: A single completed event in the future requires the present form of the perfective verb ('koupím').

quiz.question: What will you (informal singular) cook for lunch?
quiz.explanation: 2nd person singular perfective future for preparing a meal is 'uvaříš'.

quiz.question: We will wait here for you.
quiz.explanation: 'Počkáme' (perfective present) correctly signals the future commitment; 'budeme počkat' is ungrammatical.

tip: Golden rule: If a verb has a prefix making it perfective (like 'u-', 'na-', 'pře-'), NEVER put 'budu' in front of it!

title: Genitive Singular in Possession, Negation, and Prepositions
subtitle: Master the 2nd case endings for expressing belonging, origin, and absence
keyPoint: The genitive singular identifies possession, responds to common prepositions like 'do', 'od', 'z', and 'bez', and generally takes -a/-u for masculine, -y/-e for feminine, and -a/-e for neuter nouns.

useCases.label: Absence ('bez')
useCases.example: Piju kávu bez cukru a mléka.

examples.en: Dostal jsem dopis od dobrého kamaráda.
Vlak jede z Prahy do Brna.
Dnes přišel do práce bez kabátu.

mistakes.note: The preposition 'do' (into) strictly takes the genitive; neuter 'divadlo' becomes 'divadla'.
The preposition 'bez' (without) requires the genitive case ending '-u' for inanimate masculine nouns like 'cukr'.
Possession requires the genitive case on both modifier and noun ('mého otce'), not nominative.

quiz.question: We are going to Prague tomorrow. (Jdeme do ___.)
quiz.explanation: The directional preposition 'do' triggers the genitive singular; feminine 'Praha' ends in '-y' ('do Prahy').

quiz.question: He ordered tea without sugar. (Objednal si čaj bez ___.)
quiz.explanation: 'Bez' requires genitive, and masculine inanimate 'cukr' takes the ending '-u'.

quiz.question: This is the car of my sister. (To je auto mojí ___.)
quiz.explanation: Expressing possession with 'sestra' calls for the genitive singular ending '-y'.

quiz.question: She returned from work very late. (Vrátila se z ___ velmi pozdě.)
quiz.explanation: Preposition 'z' (from) takes genitive; 'práce' remains 'práce' in genitive singular (soft feminine declension).

tip: Prepositions expressing motion toward an interior ('do') or away from a surface/source ('od', 'z') ALWAYS govern the genitive case.

title: Dative Singular and Indirect Objects
subtitle: Signal giving, telling, and personal states with the 3rd case
keyPoint: The dative singular marks the recipient or beneficiary of an action and frequently uses the endings -ovi/-u for masculine, -ě/-e for feminine, and -u for neuter.

mistakes.note: Indirect recipient of speech takes the dative animate ending '-ovi', not the nominative.
Impersonal feelings and bodily states use dative pronouns ('mi', 'ti', 'mu'), literally 'It is cold to me'.
The preposition 'k / ke' (towards / to someone's place) requires the dative case.

quiz.question: I gave the flowers to my mother. (Dal jsem květiny ___.)
quiz.explanation: The recipient takes the dative case. 'Maminka' changes to 'mamince' through consonant mutation (k -> c).

quiz.question: How old is Jan? (Kolik je ___?)
quiz.explanation: In Czech, age expressions require the dative case ('Je Janovi třicet let').

quiz.question: Can you help me? (Můžeš ___ pomoct?)
quiz.explanation: The verb 'pomoct' strictly governs the dative; short dative singular pronoun for 'já' is 'mi'.

quiz.question: We are walking to the train station. (Jdeme k ___.)
quiz.explanation: The preposition 'k' takes the dative case; soft neuter noun 'nádraží' retains '-í' in dative singular.

tip: When a masculine animate noun is modified by a name or adjective, put '-ovi' on the last word (e.g., 'panu Novákovi', not 'panovi Novákovi')!

title: Instrumental Singular for Means and Predicates
subtitle: Master the 7th case for instruments, transport, accompaniment, and states of being
keyPoint: Use the bare instrumental for means, tools, and temporary predicate states after 'být', but always add the preposition 's/se' when expressing accompaniment ('with someone').

useCases.label: Means of Transport and Tools
useCases.example: Jezdím do práce autem a píšu modrým perem.

useCases.label: Accompaniment with 's/se'
useCases.example: Včera večer jsem byl v kině s Marií.

useCases.label: Predicates after 'být' and 'stát se'
useCases.example: Můj bratr se chce stát slavným právníkem.

mistakes.note: Do not use 's' for means of transport or instruments; use bare instrumental.
The preposition 's' requires the instrumental ending (-ou for feminine hard nouns).
Physical instruments of action take the bare instrumental without 's'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct means of transport: 'Do Prahy obvykle jezdím ___.'
quiz.explanation: Means of transport require the bare instrumental masculine ending -em.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for accompaniment: 'Šel jsem na večeři ___.'
quiz.explanation: Accompaniment requires the preposition 's' followed by the instrumental form 'Petrem'.

quiz.question: Complete the profession predicate: 'Petr je velmi dobrým ___.'
quiz.explanation: Predicate nouns denoting roles or professions after 'být' frequently take the bare instrumental.

quiz.question: Select the correct form for instrument: 'Babička krájí dort ostrým ___.'
quiz.explanation: The instrument of cutting takes the bare instrumental 'nožem' without any preposition.

tip: Remember: 's/se' means 'along with'. If you say 'Jedu s vlakem', it sounds like the train is walking beside you!

title: Wackernagel's Law: Clitic Pronoun Ordering
subtitle: Positioning unaccented short pronouns and auxiliaries in the second slot
keyPoint: Czech clitics (short unstressed words) cannot start a sentence and must bundle together in strict internal sequence into the absolute second syntactic position.

cells: jsem, jsi, jsme, jste / bych, bys, by
ti, mi, mu, jí, nám, vám, jim
tě, mě, ho, ji, to, nás, vás, je
Včera jsem se mu to rozhodl říct.

useCases.label: Auxiliary + Reflexive Clitic
useCases.example: Včera jsem se probudil velmi brzy.

examples.en: Včera jsem se vrátil pozdě v noci.
Proč jsi mi to neřekl dříve?
Moc se mi líbí tvoje nové auto.
Rodiče mi ho koupili k narozeninám.
Včera jsme si o tom dlouho povídali.

mistakes.note: Clitics can never stand at the absolute beginning of an independent sentence.
Within the clitic cluster, dative clitics (mu) must precede accusative clitics (to).

mistakes.wrong: Včera se jsem koupal v bazénu.
mistakes.right: Včera jsem se koupal v bazénu.
mistakes.note: Past tense auxiliary forms (jsem, jsi) always precede reflexive particles (se, si).

quiz.question: Identify the correct clitic sequence: 'Včera ___ koupil nový telefon.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'jsem' comes first, followed by the reflexive clitic 'si'.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly ordered sentence:
quiz.explanation: Following the first stress unit 'Zítra', the clitic cluster orders dative ('ti') before accusative ('to').

quiz.question: Which word order is forbidden in Czech standard grammar?
quiz.explanation: A clitic pronoun such as 'tě' cannot begin a sentence.

quiz.question: Complete the question correctly: 'Proč ___ neposlal tu zprávu?'
quiz.explanation: The past auxiliary 'jsi' must take precedence over the dative pronoun 'jí'.

tip: Think of clitics as magnets sticking tightly to the first phrase or word of the clause in the fixed sequence: Auxiliary ➔ Reflexive (se/si) ➔ Dative (mi/ti) ➔ Accusative (mě/tě/to).

title: Verbs of Motion: Determinate vs. Indeterminate
subtitle: Navigating directional vs. habitual and multi-directional movement
keyPoint: Determinate verbs (jít, jet) denote single-direction, ongoing trips happening right now, while indeterminate verbs (chodit, jezdit) denote habitual trips, round trips, or general ability.

cells: One direction, in progress right now

useCases.label: Habitual or Repeated Routine
useCases.example: Každý den chodím do školy pěšky.

useCases.label: Completed Round-trip in Past
useCases.example: V létě jsme jezdili po celé Evropě.

examples.en: Právě teď jedu vlakem do Brna.
O víkendech často chodíme do lesa.
Vlak z Prahy už přijel na nádraží.
Kam zrovna jdeš s tou taškou?

mistakes.note: Use indeterminate 'chodit' for repeated, habitual actions.
Use determinate 'jít' for motion happening in one specific direction right now.

mistakes.wrong: Včera jsme jeli pěšky do centra.
mistakes.right: Včera jsme šli pěšky do centra.
mistakes.note: 'Jet' requires a vehicle; for traveling on foot, use forms of 'jít' or 'chodit'.

quiz.question: Choose the right verb for a current action: 'Počkej na mě, právě ___ domů!'
quiz.explanation: 'Jdu' expresses an action on foot occurring right now toward a specific destination.

quiz.question: Select the correct form for repeated travel: 'Eva ___ každé léto k moři autem.'
quiz.explanation: 'Jezdí' expresses habitual, repeated motion by vehicle.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct prefixed perfective verb: 'Hosté už skončili večeři a ___ domů.'
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'od-' combined with determinate 'jít' forms 'odejít' (past plural: 'odešli'), meaning 'they departed/left'.

quiz.question: Which verb implies moving by foot, not by vehicle?
quiz.explanation: 'Chodit' specifically designates walking/traveling on foot.

tip: Ask yourself: Is it happening right now in one line (jít/jet)? Or is it a routine / back-and-forth round trip (chodit/jezdit)?

title: Conditional Mood with 'by-forms'
subtitle: Polite requests, hypothetical situations, and desires using conditional auxiliaries
keyPoint: The Czech conditional is formed by combining the past participle (-l form) with the special clitic auxiliary particles: bych, bys, by, bychom, byste, by.

useCases.label: Polite Requests and Wishes
useCases.example: Chtěl bych jeden šálek černé kávy, prosím.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Conditions ('kdyby')
useCases.example: Kdybych měl více peněz, cestoval bych.

useCases.label: Purpose Clauses with 'aby'
useCases.example: Řekl mi to, abych se nebál.

examples.en: Rád bych tě pozval na večeři.
Co bys dělal na mém místě?
Kdybychom měli čas, šli bychom do kina.
Petr by to určitě zvládl sám.

mistakes.wrong: Kdyby jsem měl peníze, koupil bych to.
mistakes.right: Kdybych měl peníze, koupil bych to.
mistakes.note: Never say 'kdyby jsem' or 'aby jsem'; merge them into 'kdybych' and 'abych'.
The second-person plural conditional particle is 'byste', written as a single word.
Standard Czech requires 'bychom' for the 1st person plural; 'by jsme' is non-standard colloquial.

quiz.question: Select the correct polite form: 'Já ___ rád sklenici vody.'
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person singular conditional auxiliary matching 'já' is 'bych'.

quiz.question: How do you correctly combine 'kdyby' + 1st person singular?
quiz.explanation: 'Kdyby' merges with 'bych' into the single word 'kdybych'.

quiz.question: Complete the polite question: 'Pane Nováku, ___ mi s tím pomoct?'
quiz.explanation: Formal address (vykání) requires the 2nd-person plural marker 'byste'.

quiz.question: Identify the standard first-person plural form: 'Zítra ___ rádi přijeli.'
quiz.explanation: 'Bychom' is the only grammatically correct standard form for the 1st person plural (we).

tip: In everyday speech you will hear 'by jsme' and 'abysme', but written and formal Czech strictly requires 'bychom' and 'abychom'.

title: Reflexive Mechanics: True Reflexives, Reciprocals, and 'se' vs. 'si'
subtitle: Navigating the crucial contrast between accusative 'se' and dative 'si'
keyPoint: Use 'se' (accusative) when the subject acts directly on itself as the direct object, and 'si' (dative) when the subject acts for its own benefit, interest, or on its own body part.

useCases.label: Direct Self-Action ('se')
useCases.example: Ráno se rychle umyju a obléknu.

useCases.label: Reciprocal Mutual Action
useCases.example: S Petrem se známe už deset let.

mistakes.note: When the object being cleaned is a body part (zuby), use dative 'si', not accusative 'se'.
Ordering food/drink for oneself requires the dative of interest 'dát si'.
The verb 'sednout si' (to sit down) lexically requires dative 'si'.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'I brush my teeth'?
quiz.explanation: Brushing one's own teeth requires the dative reflexive 'si' to indicate possession/affected body part.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for ordering: 'V restauraci ___ polévku.'
quiz.explanation: The idiom for ordering food or drink for yourself is 'dát si'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for direct reflexive action: 'Bratr se probudil a začal ___ mýt.'
quiz.explanation: 'Mýt se' means to wash oneself entirely as the direct object of the verb.

quiz.question: Complete the reciprocal sentence: 'S Janou ___ často telefonujeme.'
quiz.explanation: 'Telefonovat si' takes dative 'si' because you are calling TO each other (telefonovat někomu).

tip: If the sentence already has a direct accusative noun object (like 'zuby', 'kávu', or 'auto'), the reflexive pronoun will almost always be 'si', not 'se'!

title: Plural Noun and Adjective Declension Patterns
subtitle: Master case endings and consonant mutations across Czech plurals
keyPoint: Masculine animate nouns undergo consonant softening in the nominative plural, while oblique plural endings are largely shared across genders.

useCases.label: Consonant Mutation in Subject
useCases.example: Naši noví kolegové přišli včas do kanceláře.

useCases.label: Zero Ending in Genitive Plural
useCases.example: Máme málo volných míst a ještě méně dobrých zpráv.

useCases.label: Universal Instrumental Endings
useCases.example: Mluvili jsme se všemi těmi milými studentkami.

examples.en: Ti zkušení lékaři pracují v moderní nemocnici.
Viděli jsme mnoho krásných historických měst.
Šel na procházku se svými věrnými psy.
Všichni čeští vojáci stáli před budovou.

mistakes.note: The stem consonant 'ch' softens to 'š' before the masculine animate nominative plural ending -i.
Neuter nouns following the pattern 'město' take a zero-ending in the genitive plural, not locative -ech.

mistakes.wrong: Mluvili jsme s těmi ženami a muži.
mistakes.right: Mluvili jsme s těmi ženami a muži.
mistakes.note: Instrumental plural for masculine hard stems ends in -y (muži is correct only for soft stems like muž, but studenty for student).

quiz.question: V parku stáli dva mladí ___.
quiz.explanation: The masculine animate noun 'kluk' mutates 'k' to 'c' in the nominative plural: 'kluci'.

quiz.question: Mluvili jsme o našich nových ___.
quiz.explanation: Locative plural after the preposition 'o' takes the ending -ích for masculine animate soft stems.

quiz.question: Ve třídě je hodně malých ___.
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns like 'okno' drop their ending in genitive plural and insert a mobile 'e' yielding 'oken'.

quiz.question: Šli jsme na večeři se starými ___.
quiz.explanation: Instrumental plural requires the ending -y for masculine hard stems like 'kamarád'.

tip: Remember the big mutation rules for masculine nominative plural: k → c (Polák → Poláci), h → z (pstruh → pstruzi), ch → š (Čech → Češi), and r → ř (doktor → doktoři).

title: Numeral Syntax and Counting Dependencies
subtitle: Navigating 1 vs. 2–4 vs. 5+ and quantifying genitives
keyPoint: Numbers 2–4 require nominative plural nouns with plural verbs, while 5 and above require genitive plural nouns and neuter singular verbs.

useCases.label: Cardinal 2-4 Agreement
useCases.example: V pokoji čekaly čtyři mladé ženy.

useCases.label: Cardinal 5+ Subject & Neuter Verb
useCases.example: Na konferenci přijelo deset zahraničních delegátů.

useCases.label: Quantifier with Genitive
useCases.example: V obchodě bylo mnoho spokojených zákazníků.

examples.en: Na stole ležely tři červené jablka.
Do Prahy přijelo pět nových kolegů.
Včera tam bylo málo volného času.
Sedm malých dětí si hrálo na zahradě.

mistakes.note: Numerals 5 and above take genitive plural (studentů) and a 3rd person singular neuter verb (přišlo).

mistakes.wrong: Viděl jsem dva ženy v parku.
mistakes.right: Viděl jsem dvě ženy v parku.
mistakes.note: 'Dva' is only masculine; feminine and neuter nouns require 'dvě'.
Quantifying adverbs like 'mnoho', 'málo', or 'kolik' trigger neuter singular verb forms ('bylo').

quiz.question: Na letišti ___ šest cizích turistů.
quiz.explanation: With the cardinal numeral 'šest' (5+), the predicate must be in the 3rd person neuter singular: 'čekalo'.

quiz.question: Venku stáli ___ muži a hlasitě diskutovali.
quiz.explanation: Nominative subject for numbers 2-4 takes 'tři' with nominative plural noun 'muži' and masculine animate plural verb.

quiz.question: V naší třídě studuje ___ studentek.
quiz.explanation: 'Studentek' is in the genitive plural, which is triggered by numbers 5 and higher, such as 'patnáct'.

quiz.question: Byli jsme tam s ___ dobrými kamarády.
quiz.explanation: The preposition 's' (with) takes the instrumental case; the instrumental form of 'dva' is 'dvěma'.

tip: Think of 5+ numerals as collective buckets: grammatically, the bucket itself is singular neuter ('bylo pět...'), and everything inside it turns into genitive ('...lidí').

title: Relative Pronouns: 'který', 'jenž', and Colloquial 'co'
subtitle: Navigating standard 'který', literary 'jenž', and spoken 'co'
keyPoint: While 'který' inflects by gender and case according to its role in the relative clause, 'jenž' is its formal literary counterpart, and colloquial 'co' is indeclinable.

cells: Ten chlap, co jsem ho viděl.

useCases.label: Standard Subordinate Clause
useCases.example: To je ten spisovatel, o kterém jsme včera mluvili.

useCases.label: Literary Czech with 'jenž'
useCases.example: Dostal dopis, jehož obsah ho velice překvapil.

useCases.label: Everyday Spoken Relative Clause
useCases.example: Přišla ta holka, co s ní chodí Martin do školy.

examples.en: Auto, které stálo před domem, bylo modré.
Obdivuji vědce, jimž se podařilo najít lék.
To je ten dům, v němž jsem prožil celé dětství.
Hledám člověka, kterému mohu plně důvěřovat.
Znáš toho pána, co mu včera ukradli peněženku?

mistakes.wrong: To je ten muž, kterého jsem mluvil.
mistakes.right: To je ten muž, o kterém jsem mluvil.
mistakes.note: Relative pronouns require the exact preposition and case governed by the subordinate verb ('mluvit o kom').

mistakes.wrong: To je ta kniha, co jsem ji koupil včera. (in formal essay)
mistakes.right: To je ta kniha, kterou jsem koupil včera.
mistakes.note: 'Co + personal pronoun' is strictly colloquial; use 'kterou' or 'již' in standard written Czech.
Number must match the plural antecedent: 'studenti' requires the plural dative 'kterým', not singular 'kterému'.

quiz.question: Hledám klíče, ___ jsem položil na stůl.
quiz.explanation: 'Klíče' is inanimate masculine plural, accusative case in the relative clause requires 'které'.

quiz.question: Profesor, o ___ jsme hovořili, napsal novou studii.
quiz.explanation: After the preposition 'o' with locative, the relative pronoun 'jenž' becomes 'němž'.

quiz.question: Navštívil kamarádku, s ___ dlouho nemluvil.
quiz.explanation: Wait: 's' takes instrumental, so 'kterou' is accusative; with instrumental 'se kterou' or 's níž' is needed. But among choices, feminine instrumental is 'kterou' (historically colloquial) or accusative? For standard instrumental 'kterou' is incorrect. Let's pick 'kterou' with accusative sentence: 'Pozval kamarádku, ___ dlouho neviděl.'

quiz.question: To je ten kluk, ___ jsem včera půjčil své kolo.
quiz.explanation: The verb 'půjčit' governs the dative case (to loan to someone), requiring singular masculine dative 'kterému'.

tip: When in doubt in standard Czech, always use 'který'. Reserve 'jenž' for formal writing and journalism, and avoid 'co + clitic' in academic tests.

title: Transgressives (Přechodníky) and Verbal Adjectives
subtitle: Unlocking literary verbal adverbs for simultaneous and past actions
keyPoint: Transgressives express secondary simultaneous (imperfective) or prior (perfective) actions sharing the subject with the main verb, inflecting only for gender and number.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Action (Present)
useCases.example: Čtouc ranní noviny, popíjela horkou kávu.

useCases.label: Prior Action (Past)
useCases.example: Dopiv sklenici vody, odešel z místnosti.

useCases.label: Plural Transgressive in Literature
useCases.example: Vojáci, překročivše řeku, začali stavět tábor.

examples.en: Vraceje se domů, potkal starého známého.
Dívka seděla u okna, tiše pláčíc.
Nevědouce, co dělat, požádali o radu.
Uviděv svého otce, chlapec se usmál.
Žena, otevřivši dveře, uviděla neznámého hosta.

mistakes.wrong: Vracejíc se domů, Petr potkal bratra.
mistakes.right: Vraceje se domů, Petr potkal bratra.
mistakes.note: Petr is masculine singular, so the present transgressive requires the masculine ending '-e/-ě/-aje' (vraceje), not feminine '-íc'.

mistakes.right: Když seděl na židli, zazvonil telefon.
mistakes.note: Dangling transgressive: the transgressive subject MUST be identical to the main clause subject (the phone cannot be sitting).
The subject 'my' (we) is plural, requiring the plural transgressive ending '-vše' (udělavše).

quiz.question: Babička seděla v křesle, pletouc teplý svetr a ___ starou píseň.
quiz.explanation: 'Babička' is feminine singular, so the present transgressive takes the suffix -íc ('zpívajíc').

quiz.question: Muž, ___ dopis, vyšel ven na ulici.
quiz.explanation: The past transgressive for a masculine singular subject ending in a vowel stem takes -v ('napsav').

quiz.question: Děti, ___ na hřišti, zapomněly na čas.
quiz.explanation: 'Děti' is plural; the present transgressive plural ending is -íce ('hrajíce').

quiz.question: ___ celou pravdu, rozhodla se odejít.
quiz.explanation: Past transgressive feminine singular takes the ending -vši ('zjistivši') for prior completed actions.

tip: Transgressives are almost exclusively used in high literature and older translations; in modern spoken and normal written Czech, replace them with a temporal conjunction like 'když' or 'zatímco'.

title: Spisovná vs. Obecná Čeština Morphological Shifts
subtitle: Navigating systematic vowel and consonant shifts in everyday speech
keyPoint: Common Czech (obecná čeština) systematically replaces standard 'é' with 'ý/í', standard 'ý' with 'ej', adds prothetic 'v-' before initial 'o-', and simplifies plural instrumentals to '-ma'.

cells: ý / í → ej in roots & stems

useCases.label: Everyday Conversational Pronunciation
useCases.example: Vem si ten teplej svetr a zavři to vokno.

useCases.label: Unified Instrumental Plural in Speech
useCases.example: Mluvil jsem s těma novejma sousedama.

useCases.label: Dropped Syllabic Elements
useCases.example: Dyť já vím, že sem mu to už říkal.

examples.en: Dneska máme k obědu výborné polévky.
Dneska máme k vobědu výborný polívky.
S těma malejma dětma je spousta práce.

mistakes.wrong: Napsal jsem oficiální email s novejma informacema.
mistakes.right: Napsal jsem oficiální email s novými informacemi.
mistakes.note: Never use the colloquial instrumental '-ma' or stem diphthong '-ej-' in formal correspondence or essays.

mistakes.wrong: To je velkej problém. (in formal academic state exam)
mistakes.note: Standard Czech requires 'velký'; 'velkej' is colloquial morphology suitable only for relaxed conversation.

mistakes.wrong: Viděl jsem vobě dvě dívky. (standard text)
mistakes.note: The prothetic 'v-' before initial 'o-' is non-standard and considered an error in standard written Czech.

quiz.question: Jak zní standardní (spisovný) tvar věty 'Von tam nechce bejt'?
quiz.explanation: The standard equivalents eliminate prothetic 'v-' ('on') and change 'bejt' to standard 'být'.

quiz.question: Jaký je spisovný tvar obecněčeského výrazu 's velkejma domama'?
quiz.explanation: Standard masculine instrumental plural is 's velkými domy', dropping the colloquial '-ej-' and universal dual '-ma'.

quiz.question: Co nahrazuje obecněčeské 'pěkný počasí' ve spisovné češtině?
quiz.explanation: In standard Czech, neuter adjectives take the ending '-é' in the nominative/accusative singular ('pěkné počasí').

quiz.question: Které slovo obsahuje protetické 'v-'?
quiz.explanation: 'Vokurka' comes from standard 'okurka', where an unetymological prothetic 'v-' is added before initial 'o-'.

tip: Code-switching is ubiquitous in the Czech Republic: educated native speakers often use obecná čeština among friends, but instantly switch to spisovná čeština on television, in business, and in exams.
